clinicalPearls: Presents with grouped excoriated papules and nodules, typically on the extensor surfaces of the limbs and sometimes the trunk.
Often arises earlier than polymorphic eruption, commonly in the second trimester between around 25 and 30 weeks.
Now widely regarded as part of the atopic eruption of pregnancy spectrum, occurring in women with an atopic diathesis.
Lesions frequently show central excoriation or crusting reflecting the intense scratching that drives the picture.
Diagnosis is clinical; there are no diagnostic laboratory findings and direct immunofluorescence is negative.
Total serum IgE may be raised, reflecting the underlying atopic tendency.
It is benign for mother and fetus, with no reported increase in adverse pregnancy outcomes.
Management centres on emollients, topical corticosteroids and antihistamines, with attention to a possible atopic flare.
reference.pathophysiology: Prurigo of pregnancy is considered a manifestation of an atopic tendency unmasked or exacerbated by the immunological shift of pregnancy. The normal gestational skew from T-helper-1 towards T-helper-2 cytokine dominance favours the atopic phenotype, promoting pruritus and the prurigo reaction pattern. Repeated scratching in response to itch produces the characteristic excoriated papules and nodules through a chronic itch-scratch cycle rather than a primary blistering or autoimmune process. There is no autoantibody and no consistent hormonal trigger, and the condition overlaps clinically and conceptually with the eczematous and papular forms grouped under atopic eruption of pregnancy.
additionalDifferentials: atopic eruption of pregnancy (eczematous and papular types)
folliculitis or pruritic folliculitis of pregnancy
additionalInvestigations: serum bile acids and liver function tests to exclude obstetric cholestasis
skin biopsy if diagnosis uncertain (non-specific with parakeratosis, acanthosis and dermal inflammation)
direct immunofluorescence to exclude pemphigoid gestationis in atypical cases
skin scrapings for scabies mites where itch is severe and contacts affected
redFlags: widespread pruritus without primary lesions and abnormal bile acids indicating intrahepatic cholestasis of pregnancy
tense blisters or umbilical involvement suggesting pemphigoid gestationis
jaundice, pale stools or dark urine pointing to hepatobiliary disease
burrows, involvement of web spaces or affected household contacts suggesting scabies
signs of secondary bacterial infection of excoriated lesions
reference.prognosis: Benign and self-limiting, usually resolving in the weeks after delivery, although lesions and post-inflammatory pigmentation may persist for some weeks. There is no fetal risk, but recurrence in subsequent pregnancies can occur given the underlying atopic predisposition.
pitfalls: Attributing generalised pruritus to prurigo and failing to measure bile acids, thereby missing intrahepatic cholestasis with its fetal risk.
Overlooking scabies, which can closely mimic prurigo and requires treatment of contacts.
Undertreating pruritus so the itch-scratch cycle perpetuates nodules and secondary infection.
Regarding it as entirely distinct from atopic eruption of pregnancy and missing a broader atopic flare needing eczema care.
Confusing persistent post-delivery lesions with treatment failure rather than expected slow resolution.
